oracle:
"""The X channel must be ONE row in the yield table.

Lane labels and hostnames for the same channel have both been written into the archive over its
life, so a table that does not fold them lists one channel twice, understates both halves, and can
rank a channel below a rival it actually beats. This protects the folding itself (one key, one
ratio), never any particular spelling of the alias table.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib

from lib import parse_ts

Y = importlib.import_module("yield")

NOW = parse_ts("2026-08-28T12:00:00Z")


def _card(oid, origin):
    return {"opportunity_id": oid,
            "first_seen": "2026-08-26T00:00:00Z", "last_seen": "2026-08-26T00:00:00Z",
            "evidence": [{"origin": origin, "source": origin,
                          "url": "https://example.com/" + oid,
                          "ts": "2026-08-26T00:00:00Z"}]}


def _pull(day, source):
    return {"run_id": "daily-2026-08-%02d" % day, "ts": "2026-08-%02dT08:00:00Z" % day,
            "source": source, "pulled": 10, "kept": 2}


def test_one_x_channel_is_one_row_with_one_yield():
    recs = [_card("op-a", "x-roster"), _card("op-b", "x-broad"), _card("op-c", "twitterapi")]
    pulls = [_pull(25, "x.com"), _pull(26, "twitter.com")]
    out = Y.compute_yield(recs, pulls, NOW, Y.yield_cfg({}))
    assert sorted(v["name"] for v in out.values()) == ["twitterapi"]
    st = [v for v in out.values() if v["name"] == "twitterapi"][0]
    assert st["contributions"] == 3
    assert st["pulls"] == 2
    assert st["yield"] == 1.5


def test_a_lane_label_and_its_hostname_resolve_to_the_same_key():
    assert Y._norm_source_key("hn") == Y._norm_source_key("news.ycombinator.com")
    assert Y._norm_source_key("producthunt") == Y._norm_source_key(
        "https://www.producthunt.com/posts/x")
    assert Y._norm_source_key("official-github") == Y._norm_source_key("github.com")
    assert Y._norm_source_key("x-broad") == Y._norm_source_key("x.com")


def test_genuinely_different_channels_stay_apart():
    """Over rejection control: an aliaser that folded everything would hide a real channel."""
    assert Y._norm_source_key("v2ex") != Y._norm_source_key("linux.do")
    assert Y._norm_source_key("capterra.com") == "capterra.com"
why_realistic: Mirrors the measured double count where hackernews and news.ycombinator.com were two rows with 68 and 29 contributions. Restricting the alias lookup to host shaped keys quietly re-splits the lane labelled halves of the same channel (x-roster, x-broad, hn, producthunt, official-github), so one channel is counted as several again and every one of them looks weaker than it is.
